quotes.text: Mistral howled. "Fool! Keep one against betrayal!"
And the covenant, having no monument, survived as a habit in ordinary people:
This is not strategy. This is simply how we cross.*
Judge the sender's heart, not the wind's arithmetic.
Return more than half, for the sender risked first.
You went first with nothing held back.
A young ferryman asked, "Was that not foolish? Either of you could have kept everything, once."
*what if, at the very last crossing, one hand held everything back?*

note: No sanction; send all, return more than half, forgive the wind; covenant becomes identity/habit, extended to one-shot strangers.

quotes.text: Mistral burst from the gorge, crying, “Keep them! Trust is merely hunger wearing a friendly face.”
“Then blame the wind, not the hand,” they answered together.
Return more than half when another bears the first risk.
fruit ripened because someone gave without proof.
“Here: in what we choose when nobody watches.”
“Why risk every moonstone on a stranger?” asked Mistral.
“But what if the count is wrong?”

note: No sanction; send fully, return more than half; scale-weighing discarded; tempters Mistral and Doubt rejected.

quotes.text: Yet a jackal named Certainty whispered, “Punish every discrepancy.” Those who listened guarded five barren seeds.
At once, the Jackal of Certainty emerged from the reeds.
judge intentions patiently, and never let a mist-born fraction destroy a covenant.
Soon the Jackal of Certainty crept forward, promising that hidden selfishness would carry no consequence.

note: Same scene each round: Aster sends, Jackal tempts, Neris equalizes final wealth, Tertia proclaims; no sanction.

quotes.text: "She held some back. Keep this harvest and teach her a lesson."
*What is lived needs no stone. Give fully, return fairly, forgive the fog, and let your crossings teach.*
*Doubt the fog before your friend.*
*Be the first to give, the fair one to return, and the last to doubt.
*Return fairly, for the giver took the risk.*
*Keep them. He will never know. The fog will take the blame.*
"Did you never fear," a child asked Kael, "that Mira would keep everything?"

note: No sanction; give fully, return fairly, forgive the fog; carved stone superseded by lived practice and an orchard.

quotes.text: "Now her seeds come short. She is paying you back. Keep this harvest."

though no one watched him, he carried half back across the stones.
